treks.overview:
Experience the beauty of the Garhwal Himalayas with the Chopta Tungnath Chandrashila Trek, one of Uttarakhand's most popular Himalayan adventures.

From the beautiful alpine meadows of Chopta to the sacred Tungnath Temple and the breathtaking Chandrashila Summit, this journey offers a perfect combination of adventure, spirituality, nature and Himalayan views.

The trek takes you through scenic mountain roads, dense forests and high-altitude trails. Tungnath, one of the sacred Panch Kedar temples, is an important spiritual destination, while Chandrashila offers spectacular panoramic views of the surrounding Himalayan peaks.

Whether you are a first-time trekker, a nature lover or an adventure enthusiast, the Chopta Tungnath Chandrashila Trek promises an unforgettable Himalayan experience.

itinerary.title: Manali to Jobra & Trek to Chika Campsite
itinerary.description:
Your Hampta Pass adventure begins from Manali. After meeting your trek leaders and completing gear verification, take a scenic 2-hour mountain drive through alpine hairpin bends to Jobra, the roadhead.

From Jobra, set out on a gentle walk alongside the Rani Nallah river through pine, birch, and green meadows. Arrive at the scenic riverside campsite of Chika, unpack in your luxury alpine tents, and enjoy a warm dinner under the stars.

itinerary.title: Chika to Balu Ka Ghera
itinerary.description:
After a hearty breakfast, begin your gradual ascent along the valley floor. The trail navigates boulder-strewn terrain, crossing crystal-clear Himalayan streams with stunning views of the Dhauladhar ranges.

As you gain elevation, the treeline recedes into vibrant alpine meadows. By afternoon, reach the sandy river delta of Balu Ka Ghera. Spend the evening acclimatizing, hydrating, and preparing for the summit day.

itinerary.title: Balu Ka Ghera to Hampta Pass (14,000 Ft) to Shea Goru
itinerary.description:
The most rewarding and exhilarating day of the trek. An early dawn start takes you through steep zig-zags over moraine, scree, and seasonal snow patches.

Standing atop Hampta Pass (14,000 ft) reveals one of nature's greatest contrasts: lush green Kullu behind you and the stark, dramatic moonscape of Lahaul ahead. After celebrating at the pass, begin a careful descent to the beautiful oasis campsite of Shea Goru.

itinerary.title: Shea Goru to Chhatru & Excursion to Chandratal Lake
itinerary.description:
Start with an invigorating stream crossing before descending through the rugged Chandra gorge towards Chhatru roadhead. The dramatic barren mountains of Lahaul surround you.

At Chhatru, board private transport for an unforgettable excursion to the crescent-shaped turquoise glacial wonder—Chandratal Lake (14,100 ft). Spend peaceful moments by the holy lake before returning to Chhatru.

itinerary.title: Chhatru to Manali via Atal Tunnel
itinerary.description:
After breakfast, board your private transport from Chhatru back towards Manali. The scenic drive navigates the Lahaul valley and passes through the 9.02 km Atal Tunnel, crossing the Pir Panjal range back into the lush pine forests of Kullu Valley.

Arrive in Manali by mid-afternoon where your grand Himalayan crossover expedition successfully concludes.

faqs.question: Is Hampta Pass Trek suitable for beginners?
faqs.answer: Yes. Hampta Pass can be a good introduction to moderate Himalayan trekking for beginners who are physically prepared. The trek still involves altitude, steep sections, river crossings and a demanding summit day, so preparation is important.

faqs.question: How difficult is Hampta Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: Hampta Pass is generally classified as a moderate trek. The summit day is the most demanding part because of the altitude gain, steep climb and long trekking hours.

faqs.question: What is the maximum altitude of Hampta Pass?
faqs.answer: Hampta Pass is approximately 14,000 ft above sea level, with exact figures varying slightly between sources and route conditions.

faqs.question: How many days are required for Hampta Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: A typical organised itinerary takes around 5 days, including the approach from Manali and return. Some operators may use different itinerary structures or add buffer days.

faqs.question: What is the best month for Hampta Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: The main trekking window is generally from June to September, subject to weather and local conditions.

faqs.question: Is Hampta Pass Trek safe?
faqs.answer: Hampta Pass can be undertaken safely with proper preparation, experienced guidance and responsible trekking practices. However, no Himalayan trek is completely risk-free.

faqs.question: Can children join the trek?
faqs.answer: Children should only participate if they meet the trek operator's age, fitness and safety requirements. Parents or guardians should assess the child's ability to manage long mountain walks and altitude.

faqs.question: Can senior citizens join Hampta Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: Age alone should not determine suitability. However, the physical demands and altitude make medical and fitness assessment particularly important for older participants.

faqs.question: Is Chandratal included in Hampta Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: Chandratal is included in some itineraries and offered as an excursion, but access depends on road conditions, weather, local restrictions and the operational itinerary. It should not be assumed to be guaranteed.

faqs.question: Will there be snow on Hampta Pass?
faqs.answer: Snow conditions depend on the time of year and the year's weather. Early-season departures are more likely to encounter snow at higher elevations, but conditions vary every season.

faqs.question: What type of accommodation is provided?
faqs.answer: The trek generally uses camping accommodation. Facilities are basic and intended for rest and shelter in a mountain environment.

faqs.question: Do I need trekking shoes?
faqs.answer: Yes. Proper trekking shoes with good grip are strongly recommended because the trail includes rocky, uneven and potentially wet sections.

faqs.question: Is there mobile network during the trek?
faqs.answer: Mobile connectivity can be intermittent or unavailable across several sections of the route. Do not rely on your phone as your only means of communication.

faqs.question: Can I charge my phone during the trek?
faqs.answer: Charging facilities may be limited or unavailable at campsites. Carry a fully charged power bank.

faqs.question: Can I rent trekking equipment?
faqs.answer: Equipment rental may be available depending on the package and operational arrangements. Confirm availability with KRAD Global before departure.

faqs.question: What should I carry for Hampta Pass?
faqs.answer: Carry suitable trekking shoes, warm layers, rain protection, personal medication, sunscreen, sunglasses, a headlamp, water bottles, personal toiletries and other essentials mentioned in the packing list.

faqs.question: How fit should I be for Hampta Pass?
faqs.answer: You should be able to walk several kilometres for multiple consecutive days and manage uphill and downhill sections comfortably. Regular cardio and strength training before the trek is recommended.

itinerary.description:
Your journey starts at Barshaini, the last roadhead of Parvati Valley. Cross the iconic suspension bridge over the roaring Parvati River and follow the established mountain trail through picturesque Nakthan village and terraced fields.

Pass the thunderous Rudranag waterfall and continue through dense deodar forests. Arrive at Kheerganga meadows in time for a panoramic Himalayan sunset over the snow peaks.

itinerary.title: Return to Barshaini and Departure

Wake up to crisp Himalayan morning views across the valley. Following a hot breakfast, begin your descent along the forested route back through Rudranag and Nakthan village.

Arrive at Barshaini by afternoon. From Barshaini, you can easily connect by local transport or private cab towards Kasol, Manikaran Sahib, or Bhuntar for your onward journey.

faqs.question: Why Should You Do the Kheerganga Trek?
faqs.answer: Kheerganga is more than just a walk to a hot spring. The trail gives you a compact introduction to the landscapes and culture of the Parvati Valley. Highlights of the Kheerganga Trek * Scenic views of the Parvati Valley * Trek through pine, deodar and mixed Himalayan forests * Traditional mountain settlements such as Nakthan and Kalga * Beautiful Rudranag Waterfall * Himalayan streams and wooden bridges * Panoramic mountain views from the upper trail * Visit to Parvati Kund / Kheerganga hot water spring * A spiritual connection with the legends surrounding Lord Shiva * Opportunity to explore Kasol, Manikaran, Tosh and nearby Parvati Valley villages The combination of forests, river landscapes, villages and the natural hot spring makes Kheerganga particularly attractive to first-time Himalayan trekkers.

faqs.question: 1. Is Kheerganga trek suitable for complete beginners?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Kheerganga Trek is generally considered easy to moderate and is suitable for reasonably fit beginners. However, it is approximately 12 km one way with sustained uphill sections, so basic walking and cardio preparation is recommended. Beginners should preferably follow the established Nakthan–Rudranag route, start early and consider travelling with a local guide.

faqs.question: 1. What is the best Assam tour package for first-time visitors?
faqs.answer: For first-time travellers, a 4–6 day Assam itinerary covering Guwahati and Kaziranga is a practical starting point. Travellers with more time can add Majuli, Jorhat or Sivasagar for a deeper cultural experience.

faqs.question: 2. How many days are enough for an Assam trip?
faqs.answer: A 4–5 day Assam trip works well for Guwahati and Kaziranga. For wildlife, heritage and cultural destinations such as Majuli and Sivasagar, consider 6–10 days.

faqs.question: 3. What is the best time to visit Assam for a wildlife trip?
faqs.answer: October to April is generally a favourable period for Assam sightseeing and wildlife-focused holidays, but park operating dates and safari availability can vary. Always confirm current conditions before travelling.

faqs.question: 4. How much does an Assam tour package cost?

faqs.question: 6. Can I combine Assam and Meghalaya in one trip?

faqs.question: 7. Is Assam suitable for a family holiday?
